title: MergeMix: Optimizing Mid-Training Data Mixtures via Learnable Model Merging
claim: Conventional tuning needs ever more compute to approach optimal performance; ours reaches it at a fraction of the cost.
layout: 3 panels: two bar charts on top, conceptual cost-performance curve below
description: The figure has two rows. The top row has two bar charts. The left chart shows relative cost on a log scale for Manual, Scaling Law, CLIMB and MergeMix. The Manual bar is cut off at the top. The labels read 9.8×, 7.5× and 1.0×, and the green MergeMix bar is the lowest. The right chart compares accuracy for Manual (57.9) and MergeMix, and the green MergeMix bar is taller and runs off the top. The bottom panel is a conceptual plot. Its x-axis is computational cost in tokens, from low to high, and its y-axis is performance. Blue triangles for conventional methods follow a dashed concave curve that slowly climbs into a shaded green Optimal Performance Zone. A red star for MergeMix sits at the far left, at low cost, already inside the zone. A red annotation reads Direct Optimization via Weight Merging. The green and red highlights draw the eye to MergeMix.
caption: Cost-performance efficiency analysis. (Top) Comparison of estimated computational costs (log scale) and downstream benchmark accuracy across different data mixing strategies. Details on cost estimation are provided in Appendix [ref]. (Bottom) Conceptual illustration of the search dynamics. Conventional methods require increasing computational investment to asymptotically approach the optimal performance zone through iterative trials or fitting. In contrast, MergeMix leverages weight-space merging as an proxy, identifying the optimal mixtures with minimal cost.
abstract: Optimizing data mixtures is essential for unlocking the full potential of large language models (LLMs), yet identifying the optimal composition remains computationally prohibitive due to reliance on heuristic trials or expensive proxy training. To address this, we introduce \textbf{MergeMix}, a novel approach that efficiently determines optimal data mixing ratios by repurposing model merging weights as a high-fidelity, low-cost performance proxy. By training domain-specific experts on minimal tokens and optimizing their merging weights against downstream benchmarks, MergeMix effectively optimizes the performance of data mixtures without incurring the cost of full-scale training. Extensive experiments on models with 8B and 16B parameters validate that MergeMix achieves performance comparable to or surpassing exhaustive manual tuning while drastically reducing search costs. Furthermore, MergeMix exhibits high rank consistency (Spearman $Ï> 0.9$) and strong cross-scale transferability, offering a scalable, automated solution for data mixture optimization.
